subject: System Design
title: The Scalability Ceiling
description: Learn The Scalability Ceiling in one minute.

hook.text: You add servers, but performance stops improving. You've hit a scalability ceiling.

buildup.text: Amdahl's Law says speedup is limited by the portion of work that can't be parallelized.

discovery.text: If 10% of your workload is sequential, adding infinite servers only gives you a 10x speedup.

twist.text: Shared state, locks, and coordination create sequential bottlenecks that limit horizontal scaling.

climax.text: To break through ceilings, you must redesign the sequential parts, not just add more machines.

punchline.text: More servers can't fix a sequential bottleneck.

quiz.question: What does Amdahl's Law describe?
options: Speedup is limited by the non-parallelizable portion of work
More servers always means more speed
